title: Bergamot and vetiver room spray
subtitle: A bright, earthy room spray for living rooms and home offices
excerpt: A water-and-alcohol room spray with bergamot essential oil for a citrus top note and vetiver for a smoky, earthy base. The alcohol disperses the essential oils into a fine mist. Bergamot gives a lift; vetiver grounds it. Makes 100 ml in a small spray bottle. Shelf life 12 months.
sourceNotes: Room spray formulation: high-proof ethanol (90%+ isopropanol or perfumers' alcohol) 20-30% to dissolve and disperse EOs; distilled water 70-80%. Emulsifier (polysorbate 20 or Solubol) optional at 1-2x EO weight to prevent oil droplets on surfaces. Bergamot EO (Citrus bergamia): furocoumarin-containing; bergapten is a photosensitiser. For a room spray this is irrelevant, the spray disperses in air and is not applied to skin. Bergapten-free bergamot EO exists if skin-contact versions are needed. Vetiver EO (Chrysopogon zizanioides): distilled from root; deeply earthy, smoky, long-lasting base note. High viscosity; warm the bottle in a warm water bath before use to improve pourability. Scent ratio: bergamot 70% / vetiver 30% gives a bright citrus note with earthy foundation.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale to 200 ml easily in a standard spray bottle.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Leave to mature for 24 hours before first use, the bergamot and vetiver blend develops over that time. Shake before each use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 12 months sealed. The alcohol preserves the essential oils. The bergamot top note fades faster than the vetiver base, the spray smells progressively more earthy with age.

glossaryTerms.definition: High-purity ethanol (typically 96%+ SDA or isopropanol 90%+) used in room sprays and perfumes to dissolve essential oils and disperse them in a fine, even mist. Standard vodka is too weak to fully dissolve EOs.

In perfumery, the slowest-evaporating component of a fragrance. Vetiver is a classic base note, heavy, earthy, and persistent. It extends the life of the lighter top notes (bergamot here) and gives the blend depth.

dissolves both oils and disperses them in a fine, even mist. The bergamot lifts the room; the vetiver grounds it. Leave for 24 hours before first use for the blend to settle. Makes 100 ml; keeps 12 months.

items.prepNote: 96% ethanol; dissolves the essential oils and dries quickly
70% of essential oil total; 3% of total spray

added last; shake before each use

content.text: Combine the essential oils with the alcohol in the spray bottle. Swirl to dissolve. Vetiver is viscous, if it does not fully dissolve, place the bottle in a warm water bath (40°C) and swirl for 2 minutes.
Add the distilled water. Cap and shake well. Leave for 24 hours to mature before use.
Shake before each use. Spray into the middle of the room, not directly at surfaces or fabric.
12 months in a sealed bottle in a cool, dark cupboard. The citrus note fades first; the vetiver persists. Keep away from heat sources as the ethanol is flammable.
